historical_record.description: Built as a tobacco processing and storage warehouse for the Tobacco Company of California, to designs by William H. Crim, Jr.: three storeys of reinforced concrete under stucco, with arched bays and steel sash on a double-height ground floor, cast medallions with an Indian head on the spandrels, and an arcade along Second Street that took a rail spur.
Named a contributory building in the South End Historic District when the district was listed in Article 10 of the Planning Code.
A garment factory was the last industrial tenant; the building stood empty from 1993 or 1994.
An existing manufacturing building stood on the site.
The City Planning Commission approved the conditional use authorization to convert a historic industrial building into 35 dwelling units.

unknowns: The assessor's roll dates the structure on this parcel to 2007; the building went up in 1913.
